framework_notes: Django is the primary framework (score 1.00 >= 0.75 threshold); references/django.md was loaded in addition to references/python.md and references/patterns.md.

IMPORTANT scope fact: this CodeQL database contains ONLY the Django framework source (django/ package, its internal tests, and repo-root dev tooling). There is no user/application business code (no project-level settings module, no app views). Any Django-shaped SSRF usually lives in application views; those are absent here, so source extraction must anchor on the framework's own request boundaries instead of application route handlers.

The framework's genuine server-side HTTP fetches are exactly two: contrib/sitemaps ping_google() -> urlopen() and core/management/templates.py TemplateCommand.download() -> urlretrieve(). Neither is reachable from an inbound HTTP request inside this source tree: ping_google is driven by the `ping_google` management command (django/contrib/sitemaps/management/commands/ping_google.py reads options['sitemap_url']), and the template download is driven by the `startproject/startapp --template` CLI option. The LLM labeling step must treat these as CLI-originated fetches.

HttpRequest parsing internals (django/http/request.py get_host/build_absolute_uri, django/core/handlers/{wsgi,asgi}.py) derive URL components (scheme/host/path) from client-supplied headers (Host, X-Forwarded-Host via USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST, request line). These are extracted as source candidates (host-derived URL construction), not sinks.

HttpResponseRedirect / shortcuts.redirect / django.contrib.redirects produce HTTP redirect RESPONSES (client-side navigation), not server-side network requests; per the task contract they are NOT recorded as CWE-918 sinks (they belong to Pass 9 / CWE-601).

Third-party network clients (psycopg2, mysqlclient, sqlite3, python-memcached/pymemcache, redis, django-redis, geoip2) are external dependencies; their connect() calls happen inside library code that is not part of this database, so settings-driven DB/cache network endpoints are invisible to extraction here

The database contains framework code only - no application views/settings exist, so application-level URL preview/proxy/import endpoints (the usual Django SSRF shape) cannot be extracted; coverage is necessarily limited to the framework's own fetch sites (sitemaps ping, management template download, SMTP backend)

URL parsing helpers (urlparse/urlsplit/urljoin/validators.URLValidator) are recorded as URL-construction surfaces in repo_survey but intentionally not extracted as sinks; they only become interesting if flow analysis ties them to the two real fetch sites

HttpRequest internals that consume self.META / self.environ inside django/http/request.py and django/core/handlers/*.py are covered via the environ/scope constructor-parameter source families rather than per-field internal reads
